question.text: An Indian portfolio company is about to pay interest of INR 60 lakh on its NCDs to Ganga Infra Trust (Cat I AIF, SEBI registered). Ordinarily, interest payments attract TDS under Section 194A. What is the correct treatment for payment to the AIF?

answer.text: No TDS by the portfolio company, because CBDT notification under Section 197A(1F) exempts the AIF from TDS on non-business income received from its investees; instead, the AIF withholds under Section 194LBB when distributing to LPs.
TDS at 10% under Section 194A applies as usual.
TDS at 40% as the AIF is treated as a foreign company.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 197A(1F) read with CBDT Notification No. 51/2015 (dated 25 June 2015) provides that the payer of non-business income to an Investment Fund is NOT required to withhold tax. This prevents a cash-flow mismatch (fund receiving post-TDS interest and then having to withhold AGAIN when distributing). Tax leakage is pushed to the distribution stage under Section 194LBB (10% for residents; rate-in-force / DTAA for NRs). The Trap: Options A, B and D all apply a wrong withholding at the portfolio-company-to-AIF leg. The design intention is exactly to AVOID double withholding. Managers who forget to give the 197A(1F) confirmation to their portcos sometimes see wrongful deductions. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 197A(1F)/194LBB interplay. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) receives interest directly into client demat so 194A applies. XIX-A uses this in LP education. XV (RA) touches on withholding economics when modelling NCD returns. Manager's Pro-Tip: Give every portfolio company a copy of your AIF's 197A(1F) exemption declaration plus the CBDT notification at the time of issue closing. Follow up after the first coupon — some company CFOs default to 194A out of habit and you'll spend the year recovering refund credits.
